propositions: Plan review produces a clean PASS when child enumeration or per-child fetch fails during context assembly, because _assemble_context_uncached silently swallows exceptions and leaves children empty, making has_children return False and suppressing container-scoped DET checks.
PlanContext lacks fields to signal that hierarchy loading was incomplete, so no verdict path can detect or represent the incompleteness to downstream consumers.

The five finalize_verdict call sites (plan_review_precheck, plan_review_coach, _recover_plan_review_coach_failure, _recover_plan_review_verify_failure, _degraded_plan_review_verdict) use different plumbing (real pctx vs ctx.inputs dict vs precheck dict) to source coverage flags, creating inconsistent threading of any new hierarchy-incomplete signal.

plan-review.yaml's four plan_review_coach invocations lack inputs to receive hierarchy_incomplete and hierarchy_incomplete_detail from precheck, so ctx.inputs.get(..., False) always defaults to False even after plan_review_precheck records the signal.

Drift-floor and xcheck verdict-drop paths (_recompute_verdict_after_drop) re-derive verdicts without consulting hierarchy_incomplete, allowing a dropped BLOCK to revert to PASS despite incomplete context.

Parent epic AC #4 requires INDETERMINATE (not PASS) when hierarchy is incomplete, unless omitted context is demonstrably irrelevant — but suppressed container-scoped criteria mean no safe relevance carve-out exists, so fail-closed always-INDETERMINATE is the correct implementation.
